title: St Joseph (19 March)
hookLine: the quiet carpenter, patron of workers and fathers

lines: HE DREAMS. HE GETS UP. HE GOES.
A FEAST FOR A SILENT MAN.
cards: Go through the Gospels looking for a single sentence spoken by Joseph, the husband of Mary. You'll come up empty. He has dreams.
He gets up in the night. He takes a pregnant fiancée into his home, walks a family to Egypt and back, searches the city for a missing twelve-year-old. The text never once records him saying a word.
Mary speaks. Simeon speaks. Angels speak.
Joseph acts. After the stories of Jesus's childhood, he never appears in a scene again. Churches still give him a feast day.

teach.h: A JUST MAN, MINDED TO SPARE HER SHAME.
teach.b: Matthew's story of Joseph opens at a painful moment. Mary, the woman he's promised to, is pregnant, and not by him.
The King James Bible says: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
Before any angel, his first instinct is to spare her shame, quietly. Then an angel comes in a dream and tells him not to be afraid to take Mary as his wife.

teach.h: RAISED FROM SLEEP, HE DID AS BIDDEN.
teach.b: All Matthew gives of his response is this: "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife." No speech. No argument.
He wakes up and does it. The pattern repeats. Another dream: take the child and flee.
Matthew says he arose and took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt. Up in the dark, packing, gone. Later, when the danger is over, home again.
In his home town, people later ask about Jesus, "Is not this the carpenter's son?" The Greek word behind carpenter means a builder or craftsman, someone who works with his hands.
Mark calls Jesus himself the carpenter, so tradition pictures him learning the trade from this quiet man. That's why Catholics in particular honor Joseph as patron of workers, fathers and families.
Some Orthodox and Protestant Christians honor him too, as the righteous man who sheltered the holy family. The picture is of faith that shows up mostly as getting up and doing the next thing.

how: Catholics keep the solemnity of St Joseph in March, and in parts of Italy and among Italian-American families, St Joseph's tables of food are set out and shared with the poor; Anglicans and some Lutherans also keep his day.

o: the dreamer of Genesis, sold into Egypt by his brothers
the apostle who wrote down the Sermon on the Mount
Mary's husband, who acts in the Gospels but never speaks

did as the angel had bidden

s: Joseph has several speeches in the Gospels
the Gospels don't record a single word from him. he acts.
Joseph planned to protect Mary from public shame even before the angel came
"not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."

tektōn: someone who works with his hands, wood or stone.

games.q: you're Joseph. the woman you're promised to is pregnant, and not by you. you could make it public. what do you do?
o: make it public so everyone knows it wasn't you.
end it quietly, to spare her shame.
games.why: Matthew says he was minded to put her away privily, quietly, to spare her. then the angel came, and he took her as his wife.

practice: Think of someone who looked after you and mostly showed up rather than talked: your father, if that's a good place to go, or a grandfather, an uncle, a coach, a neighbor who once fixed your bike and asked nothing for it.
Let one thing they did come back clearly, and if you pray, thank God for them by name; if not, hold the memory with gratitude.

wordCard.voice: St Joseph. The husband of Mary and the carpenter of Nazareth, who in the Gospels never speaks, and keeps getting up to do what he was asked.
